correctness.rationale: Each odd column is a rung and its row-swap orbit cannot be in an invariant independent simplex, while the n even-column orbits are pairwise independent; fixed geometric space F_n is exactly the simplex Delta^{n-1}, contractible. Chandrakar–Singh Theorem 3.1 proves the ordinary independence complex is S^n wedge S^n. After barycentric subdivision, relative simplices outside fixed F_n occur in free two-element orbits; C_*(X_n,F_n) is a bounded free chain complex over R=Z[C2], with only homology M of integral rank two in degree n. Tensor with trivial Z computes orbit quotient relative chains. The Tor spectral sequence collapses to Tor^R_p(Z,M)=H_{n+p}(Y,F) for p>=0. Bounded dimension gives eventual Tor zero; two-periodic cyclic-group resolution forces all positive Tors to vanish. Lefschetz fixed Euler=1 gives trace zero on rank-two M; primitive invariant vector yields h e=e, h f=a e-f, and Tor_1 vanishing excludes even a, so the integral involution lattice is the regular R. Hence H_n(Y,F)=Z and other relative homology vanishes. For n>=2 Armstrong with fixed-point action on simply connected original gives pi_1(Y)=0, then integral homology plus Hurewicz/Whitehead implies Y~=S^n. n=1 has a barycentrically subdivided quotient with 9 vertices, 15 edges and six 2-cells, each removable by distinct free edge, yielding connected rank-one graph; the actual source verifier was inspected for the explicit deterministic collapses. Finite quotient homology is not used to prove n>=2. A separate from-scratch enumeration of the n=1 C6 independence simplices, their barycentric-flag C2 orbit quotient, and successive free-edge removal independently reproduced its initial 9 vertices, 15 edges, six triangles and six collapse pairs, leaving a connected 9-edge/9-vertex graph homotopy S^1.
